title: Microsoft blinked a little in the AI capex race. Wall Street loved it.
excerpt: Wall Street sent Big Tech a new message: AI spending alone isn't enough. Microsoft's restraint sparked a massive stock rally.
content_html:
By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

For several years, Big Tech has operated under a simple rule: spend more on AI, or investors will assume you're falling behind. This earnings season, that rule may have changed.

Even a year ago, if one of the cloud giants had merely held its AI spending plans steady while rivals kept increasing theirs, Wall Street probably would have panicked. Investors would have assumed AI demand was cooling or that the company had lost confidence in its competitive position.

Instead, Microsoft did exactly that this week, and its stock exploded higher — adding the most market value in one day by any US company in history.

Late Wednesday, the company kept its 2026 capital spending plan unchanged. (It actually fell from $190 billion to $175 billion due to an accounting tweak).

Meanwhile, Google added another $15 billion to its forecast, Amazon increased 2026 spending by $20 billion, and Meta boosted its plans, too.

The contrast is even starker once you look beneath the headline numbers. Memory chip prices have soared, which has pushed capex even higher. Microsoft isn't immune to this. That means its decision to hold spending steady is arguably more cautious than it first appears. If memory costs are rising while your overall budget stays flat, less money is left over for actually building those AI data centers.

And yet, investors loved it. When CFO Amy Hood outlined the conservative spending plan on a call with analysts, Microsoft shares immediately surged.

By the end of Thursday, the stock was up 15%, Microsoft's best day on the market in almost two decades. Strong Azure growth and surging Copilot adoption helped. But investors were mostly enthused by evidence that someone is thinking hard about returns, not just spending.

Before earnings season, I wondered whether any of the tech giants would blink in the race. Microsoft blinked a little, and Wall Street applauded.

content_html_zh:
作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

多年来，大型科技公司一直遵循一个简单的规则：在人工智能上投入更多资金，否则投资者会认为你落后了。 在本财报季，这一规则可能会发生变化。

即使在一年前，如果其中一家云巨头只是保持其人工智能支出计划稳定，而竞争对手则不断增加其支出计划，华尔街可能会感到恐慌。 投资者可能会认为人工智能需求正在降温，或者该公司对其竞争地位失去了信心。

相反，微软本周确实做到了这一点，其股价暴涨——成为美国历史上单日市值最高的公司。

周三晚间，该公司维持 2026 年资本支出计划不变。 （由于会计调整，它实际上从 1,900 亿美元下降到 1,750 亿美元）。

与此同时，谷歌在预测上又增加了 150 亿美元，亚马逊将 2026 年支出增加了 200 亿美元，Meta 也提高了计划。

一旦你仔细观察标题数字，对比就会更加明显。 存储芯片价格飙升，导致资本支出进一步上升。 微软也不能幸免。 这意味着其保持支出稳定的决定可以说比最初看起来更加谨慎。 如果内存成本不断上升，而总体预算保持不变，那么用于实际构建这些人工智能数据中心的资金就会减少。

然而，投资者却喜欢它。 当首席财务官艾米·胡德（Amy Hood）在与分析师的电话会议上概述保守的支出计划时，微软股价立即飙升。

截至周四收盘，微软股价上涨了 15%，这是微软近二十年来市场表现最好的一天。 Azure 的强劲增长和 Copilot 采用率的激增起到了帮助作用。 但投资者大多对有人认真考虑回报而不仅仅是支出的证据感到兴奋。

在财报季到来之前，我想知道是否有科技巨头会在竞争中眨眼。 微软眨了眨眼，华尔街鼓掌。
